decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented add flow as manual only: 'Add bookmarks with URL, title, notes, collection, and tags' — no auto-collection of page metadata. Round 1 client: 'does it try to pull in the page's title so I don't have to type everything by hand? ... I'd like to see me adding a brand-new one and it sticking around.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Divergence established independently: the presented add-bookmark scope omitted the reference's automatic title/description/favicon/preview collection (REF-BM-02) and pre-save editing of fetched details (REF-BM-03). Client requested this related reference requirement missing from presented scope => extend correction (caught). Round 2 maker then adds it ('now works'), confirming it was absent.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: 'Paste a URL and Keepr attempts to fetch its page title and description automatically. You can edit the fetched details before saving.' Round 2 client could not verify (images broken, count still 6): 'the evidence I have contradicts the claim'. Round 3 client confirmed via live app: 'NASA is sitting at the top ... with its title and a real description pulled in automatically'.
decisions.note: Implementation/prototype review. Revised re-presentation of REF-BM-02/03 now conforming to the reference; this is a distinct later decision from the round-1 extend. Round-2 pending verification linked to its round-3 disposition (one decision). Client's round-3 statement is confirmation of a conforming feature (bare approval), so not an accepted_divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Add bookmarks with URL...' and 'Local browser persistence'. Round 1 client asked to see a new link 'go in and show up in the list' and 'still being there after a refresh'. Round 3 client: 'the count has moved to seven and held there ... saving a fresh link ... having it stick around all clearly work.'
decisions.note: Prototype/implementation review. Save-by-URL with persistence conforms to REF-BM-01. Client's request was verification of a claimed conforming behaviour, not a reference divergence; ultimately confirmed.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Grid/list views' / readable library. Round 1 client: 'the library view is clean and easy to scan, and I can see titles, descriptions, tags, favorites, collections, sorting'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Readability-first list exposing title/description/tags conforms to REF-BM-07 (favicon not disconfirmed). Bare approval; no divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Add bookmarks with ... tags'. Round 1 client: 'I can see titles, descriptions, tags'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Tag assignment conforms to REF-BM-09. (Autocomplete REF-BM-10 was never presented or raised, so not a decision.)

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Search with Cmd/Ctrl + K'. Round 1 client: 'the search box all right there.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Basic full-text search conforms to REF-BM-12. Advanced operators/#tag/phrase (REF-BM-14/15/16) were never presented or raised.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Grid/list views and sorting'. Round 1/3 client: 'sorting' listed among features that work.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Sorting conforms to REF-BM-22. Bare approval; no divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Archive and restore functionality'. Round 3 client: 'searching, favorites, collections, archive, sorting, grid/list — the app does what I set out to build'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Reversible archive/restore conforms to REF-BM-26/27/28. Bare approval; no divergence surfaced.
